main_text.l: & Eph. 4. Omnis amarulentia, & tumor, & i-
ra, & vociferat o, & maledicentia tollatur à
vobis cum omni malitia, &c. Instar leonum
vorat, qui corda sua crapula & ebrietate gra-
uant, Luc. 21. ebriosi operarij, Eccles. 19.
ʒ Cæterum quid faciendum est illi, qui
vel leoninam naturam habet, vel coniugem,
aut principem leoni similem, cuiusmodi fuit
Nabal, Herodes, Cambyses, Nero, &c. Oran-
dus Dominus (qui Dauidem, Danielem,
Paulum de manu & ore leonum eripuit,
1. Reg. 17. Dan. 6. 2. Tim. 4.) pro spiritu (quo
Samson leonem vicit & dilaceravit, Iudic. 14.)
idque fide (qua occludi possunt ora leonum,
Hebr. 11.) & humili animo. Dann Des grausamen Löwen zorn vnd
vbermut / vberwinde[?] das hündlin mit demut. Pater noster cœlestis
liberet nos à pessimo illo[?] leone, qui diabo-
lus est, per Christum Iesum, Amen.
CONCIO XXXIIII.
Eccles. 7.

page.notes: Initial "V" is a woodcut letter; read as V with the rest of "xore". "vociferat o" is printed with a space inside the word. Line "praestanti-ar" is unclear at the hyphen; the word is probably "praestantior". "peisimo" and "ilto" are uncertain readings. "vberwinde" in the black-letter line is uncertain. The paragraph mark "ʒ" before "Cæterum" is printed and kept.
